News

Market and Prices

July 13, 2026

High prices likely to persist: Lavazza warns that coffee prices will remain elevated for the next two years due to ongoing market volatility, despite expectations of a strong Brazilian harvest.

Tariff concerns: The National Coffee Association (NCA) is pushing for an exemption on instant coffee from potential Brazil tariffs. Royal Coffee is issuing credits to customers affected by recent IEEPA tariffs as duties are returned.

Broader industry pressure from record-high commodity prices, which haven't fully resolved sustainability challenges (per the 2026 Coffee Barometer).

Industry & Business

Nestlé's big investment: Nestlé is investing around $696 million (CHF 563 million) in a new Nescafé production facility in Thailand to expand RTD and other capacity in Southeast Asia.

Labor shortages ahead: A major concern for future tropical plantations (coffee, cocoa, palm oil) is who will tend them amid demographic and workforce shifts.

European impact: The coffee sector generates €84.4 billion and supports 3.8 million jobs across the EU27.

News Grind

Arabica coffee futures traded around $3.1 per pound, a level not seen since March, as traders weighed signs of tightening inventories while monitoring the pace of Brazil's harvest. Arabica certified stocks at ICE fell by another 3,069 bags to 377,465, the lowest level since March 2024. In the same period last year, the volume was 841,173 bags, a reduction of 463,708 bags in twelve months. The market also factored in delays to Brazil’s harvest due to rainfall in major producing areas, alongside quality concerns, with investment funds increasing activity amid weather uncertainties. Coffee harvest in Brazil reached 44% as of June 24, below 51% a year earlier and the five-year average of 47%, according to Safras & Mercado. Meanwhile, Climatempo indicated that dry weather is expected to prevail in the first half of July, supporting harvest and post-harvest activities, with no forecast of rainfall as frequent as in June. (Trading Economics)

News

July 2026

Market Snapshot

Coffee (Arabica) futures have been volatile but recently hit multi-week highs before some pullback, trading around the $300/lb range in early July.

World Coffee Champions Crowned in Brussels: Nas Jaafar (Malaysia) won the World Brewers Cup, Andy Philein (China) took the World Coffee in Good Spirits Championship, and Benjamin Brassart (Belgium) claimed the World Coffee Roasting Championship.

Arabica Prices Seeing Strong Gains: Recent reports highlight the largest gains in four years amid market volatility.

Tariff Relief for Importers: Royal Coffee is issuing IEEPA Tariff Credits to customers for duties paid during a 2025 tariff period. U.S. Customs and Border Protection is processing refunds following court rulings.

Industry & Business Moves: Illycaffè Partners with Westrock: The Italian giant signed a multi-year deal with Arkansas-based Westrock Coffee Company for North American production and packaging.

Sustainability Check: The 2026 Coffee Barometer notes that record-high commodity prices haven't fixed deeper structural issues in the industry.

Other Notables: Backyard Beans expanding into more Giant stores; Scooter’s Coffee breaking ground on a major Nebraska distribution center; Java Factory chasing a Guinness record with 52 weekly flavors.

Fun & Emerging Trends:

Coffee in Sicily? Warming climates are enabling experimental coffee growing in Italy, with Palermo roaster Morettino leading efforts.

Decaf Gets Some Love: Recent studies and discussions explore better decaf options and potential health/gut-brain benefits of regular coffee.

Equipment Buzz: Muvna launched a modular "Mammoth" grinder; Marco brought its automated MilkPal system to the U.S.

News

Coffee On Stock Market: Prices

Arabica coffee futures traded around $2.70 per pound, near their lowest since November 2024, on expectations of a bumper harvest in top grower Brazil. Prices are down more than 20% this year, driven by improved production forecasts for Brazil’s output from several leading consultancies, following the decline in production in 2025. Despite a reportedly slow start to the harvest in some producing regions, the crop is progressing without major issues and could deliver a record output, helping replenish global coffee supplies. Brazil’s Conab recently raised its 2026/27 coffee production forecast to a record 66.7 million bags from 66.2 million in February, an 18% increase from the previous season. Arabica output is projected at 45.8 million bags, up 28% year on year and the third-largest on record, supported by a positive biennial cycle and favorable weather conditions. Rabobank said that, unless a major weather event occurs, the market will gradually enter a phase of large surplus. (Trading Economics)

News

Cafe culture remains vibrant in Australia despite economic headwinds

Australia Highlights

Strong global recognition: Australian cafes continue to punch above their weight. Multiple Aussie venues ranked in the World's 100 Best Coffee Shops 2026, with strong showings in Sydney (several spots), Melbourne, and Brisbane. Australia placed second only to the US in some tallies.

People's Choice favourites: Time Out's 2026 awards highlighted local winners like Savoir French (Canberra, ACT) and others across states as voted by Aussies.

Cost pressures: Takeaway coffee sales have slowed due to living costs, fuel prices, and economic caution. Many cafes report reduced spending, with average willingness to pay around $6.60. Latte prices in places like Melbourne have hit $7–7.50 in some suburbs, sparking debate. Higher wages and operating costs keep prices elevated even as global bean prices ease somewhat.

Market growth: The Australian cafe sector is projected to grow, driven by demand for quality convenience, sustainability, and premium experiences (e.g., McCafe expansions).technavio.comViral incident: An Australian man was arrested in Da Nang, Vietnam, after an alleged shirtless rampage at Ge Cafe. He caused significant damage (estimated ~VND500 million / ~A$26k) by smashing equipment, windows, and items with a chair. The cafe owners declined donations despite public support.

International Cafe & Coffee Business News:

Tim Hortons big investment: The Canadian chain and its owners are pouring CA$400 million (~US$290M) into 2026 — building 80 new stores and renovating 400 others.

Health perk: A large meta-analysis links low-to-moderate coffee intake to a modestly lower risk of heart failure.

Challenges & closures: Some independent cafes face rising rents, cost-of-living squeezes, and competition, leading to closures or cutbacks in various markets. On the flip side, expansions and new openings continue in places like Indiana and Vancouver.

Industry trends: Focus on climate-resistant coffee hybrids (e.g., Libex), sustainability, new equipment, and non-coffee items to drive afternoon sales. Chains like Starbucks are tweaking strategies amid softer traffic.

Inspired by their travels, the brand offers single-origin beans (Colombia, Ethiopia, Ecuador) and unique flavored blends like Watermelon Candy and Chocolate Strawberry, available online and at Dayglow locations.

April 2026

Market & Production Outlook

Record harvests ahead: Analysts project strong global coffee production for the 2026/27 season, potentially reaching a record 182.5 million bags according to StoneX forecasts. Brazil is expected to lead with a massive rebound (up ~20%+ year-on-year in some estimates), supported by favorable weather and improved flowering. This shift from recent deficits has contributed to easing price pressures, though arabica futures remain somewhat elevated amid lingering uncertainty.

Price shifts: After volatility in 2025 (with peaks driven by supply concerns), the market is pivoting toward potential surplus. Brazil's official agency (Conab) has projected a bumper 66.2 million bag harvest for 2026/27. Some observers are comparing it to cocoa's recent crash, though demand dynamics differ—high prices have already prompted some cost-cutting and softer consumer demand in places

Major Industry Moves

Nestlé selling Blue Bottle: Nestlé has confirmed the sale of premium roaster Blue Bottle Coffee to Centurium Capital (the largest shareholder in China's Luckin Coffee). This marks a notable shift for the specialty segment.

Luckin Coffee expansion: The Chinese chain claims to have opened the world's largest roastery in Qingdao, complete with what it calls the biggest roasting machine. Luckin continues aggressive growth in its home market.

Deforestation mapping initiative: Major coffee brands are partnering on new efforts to map coffee farms and combat deforestation, timed ahead of stricter EU regulations (EUDR). This ties into broader sustainability pushes across the supply chain.

Historic Closure in California:

The Original Saugus Cafe, claimed to be the oldest restaurant in Los Angeles County (established in 1886), is set to close its doors permanently on January 4, 2026, after 139 years of operation. The announcement highlighted its role in creating memories across generations.

Chinese Giant Enters US Market: Mixue, the world's largest restaurant chain by location count (known for affordable coffee and ice cream), recently opened its first US store in Los Angeles, targeting budget-conscious consumers amid ongoing inflation.

New Openings and Themed Cafés Worldwide:

Singapore is buzzing with fresh spots, including the arrival of Hong Kong's Elephant Grounds (opening January 10) and a limited-time Hangyodon-themed café starting January 7.

Hong Kong welcomes five new coffee shops this month, featuring in-house pastries, unique interiors, and ice drip specialties.

In the US, look for new cafés like Dear Donna in Kansas City and Wildgrain's café/test kitchen in Somerville (late January).

Helsinki Airport will debut an iconic Fazer Café in early 2026, offering classic Finnish pastries and handcrafted items.

Heartwarming Stories:Reinne's Place in Long Beach, California, opened as a tribute to the owner's late girlfriend, quickly becoming a community space for healing and connection.

Industry Trends and Expansions for 2026:

Rising chains like Dutch Bros (planning 175 new locations), 7 Brew, Black Rock Coffee Bar, and Bad Ass Coffee are poised for major growth across the US.

Focus on sustainability (eco-packaging, reduced single-use items), tech integration (AI personalization, mobile ordering, subscriptions), and experiential spaces (events, co-working).

Food pairings are evolving with protein-packed items, nostalgic flavors, and multi-sensory menus to boost café profits beyond coffee sales.

From Farm to Cup

Coffee harvesting season is in full swing in many regions, with challenges from weather impacts underscoring the fragile supply chainHealth Benefits Highlighted in New StudiesRecent research is brewing good news for coffee lovers:Drinking caffeinated coffee may reduce the risk of atrial fibrillation recurrence by nearly 40% in some patients.

Moderate intake (3-4 cups daily) could support longevity, slow premature aging linked to psychiatric conditions, and lower risks of chronic diseases.

More than 2 billion cups are consumed worldwide daily—science suggests many of them might be doing more good than you think!

Industry Moves and Expansions

Mixue, the massive Chinese coffee and tea chain, opened its first U.S. store in Los Angeles, targeting affordable drinks amid inflation.

Two Oregon-based coffee roasters announced a merger under a new parent company to pool resources and cut costs.

The Specialty Coffee Association revealed qualified sponsors for the 2026-2027 World Barista Championship, kicking off a new cycle of competitions.

Arabica coffee, the premium variety accounting for about 60-70% of global production, is traded primarily on the Intercontinental Exchange (ICE) as the "Coffee C" contract. Prices are quoted in US cents per pound (e.g., 355 cents = $3.55/lb).

Recent trading range: 345-358 cents/lb.

This follows volatility, with prices dipping to multi-month lows near $3.45/lb in late December amid improving supply signals, but recovering on short-covering and weather concerns.

News

Canna Cafe:

Canna Cafe refers to several establishments, mostly cannabis-themed cafés offering infused drinks, edibles, or consumption lounges (often using hemp-derived cannabinoids like Delta-8/9, CBD, or THC where legal). There's also one unrelated non-cannabis spot.

Here are some notable ones:

Canna Cafe (Chicago, IL) — A members-only cannabis café in the West Loop (1301 W Washington Blvd), known for THC-infused food and drinks. It's Black-owned and has expanded to locations in Los Angeles and Atlanta.

The Canna Cafe & Bar (Rockford, IL) — A cozy lounge offering food, mocktails, and infusions with hemp-derived cannabinoids (Delta-8, Delta-9, etc.). Located at 6830 Spring Creek Road, it's focused on education and relaxed vibes.

Café Canna (Asheville, NC) — A non-alcoholic bar with kava, kratom, specialty coffees, and cannabis-related vibes/events.

Other variations include cannabis-infused coffee pod brands (like CannaCafe Keurig pods) or similar spots in places like Thailand. There's also a completely unrelated Café Canna on the remote Isle of Canna in Scotland—a charming seafood restaurant with no cannabis connection.

News

Movies Set in or About Cafes/Coffee Shops

Many films feature cafes as central settings for drama, romance, or quirky stories. Here are some standout ones:

Amélie (2001) → A whimsical Parisian tale centered around a cafe waitress who secretly helps others.

Café (2011) → An indie drama (starring Jennifer Love Hewitt) almost entirely set in a West Philadelphia cafe, exploring interconnected lives and a metaphysical twist.

Bagdad Cafe (1987) → A touching German-American film about a stranded tourist transforming a remote desert cafe/motel.

Café Society (2016) → Woody Allen's romantic comedy/drama set in 1930s Hollywood and New York high-society nightlife.

Coffee and Cigarettes (2003) → Jim Jarmusch's anthology of short conversations in cafes.

Before the Coffee Gets Cold (Japanese series/films) → Time-travel stories in a magical Tokyo cafe.

Iconic cafe scenes appear in films like Pulp Fiction, When Harry Met Sally, You've Got Mail, and Inception.

Nov 2025

Nov 16

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

Brazilian coffee, beef and tropical fruit will still be tariffed 40%, says Brazil’s vice president

RIO DE JANEIRO — Brazilian Vice President Geraldo Alckmin said Saturday that Brazilian exported goods to the U.S. including coffee, beef and tropical fruits would still be tariffed 40%, despite President Donald Trump’s decision to remove some import taxes.

In a dramatic move on Friday, Trump scrapped levies announced in April on what he called ‘Liberation Day’ in hopes of encouraging domestic production and lifting the U.S. economy. Brazil at the time was hit with a 10% tariff.

But in July, Trump imposed a further 40% tariff, citing — among other reasons — the trial of his ally, former President Jair Bolsonaro, which he called a “witch hunt.” Proceedings went ahead regardless and in September Bolsonaro was sentenced to 27 years and three months in prison for attempting a coup.

Alckmin said some products, such as orange juice, would now have a zero tariff as they were not targeted by the additional 40%. But that extra tariff remains in place on products including coffee, beef and tropical fruits, such as mangos and pineapples.

While Brazil’s vice president welcomed Trump’s latest decision, which he called “positive” and a “step in the right direction,” he said there remained a “distortion that needs to be corrected.”

“Everyone got 10% less, but in Brazil’s case, which had 50%, we ended up with 40%, which is very high,” Alckmin told journalists in the capital Brasilia.

Alckmin said that Friday's decision means that 26% of Brazilian goods are now entering the U.S. without additional tariffs. That's up from 23%.

Trump’s July decision, which was overtly political as Brazil has a trade deficit with the United States, led to the worst U.S.-Brazil relations in history.

Those relations have since improved, and in October Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Trump met in Malaysia.

“President Lula’s conversation with President Donald Trump was important in terms of dialogue and negotiation,” Alckmin said on Saturday.

After that encounter, Lula said he was confident the two countries would soon reach a trade deal.

U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and Brazil’s Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira met for 50 minutes this week to further the conversation.

The Trump administration has insisted that its tariffs helped fill government coffers and weren’t a major factor in higher prices at grocery stores around the country. But Democrats were quick to paint Friday’s move as an acknowledgment that Trump’s policies were hurting American pocketbooks.

Record-high beef prices have been a particular concern, and Trump had said he intended to take action to try and lower them. Trump’s tariffs on Brazil, a major beef exporter, had been a factor.

Back in Brazil, the Brazilian Association of the Coffee Industry said it would continue to monitor the situation.

“(We) will keep working to ensure legal certainty, competitiveness, and predictability for the Brazilian coffee industry,” the group’s president, Pavel Cardoso, said in a statement. (Wires, A.I News)

Unsloth has released Dynamic 3.0 GGUFs for Qwen3.8-27B, with the smallest quantized file now weighing just 6.2GB.

If you downloaded an earlier Unsloth GGUF, you’ll need to download the new model files to benefit from Dynamic 3.0. This isn’t an update you can activate with a runtime flag.

Here are the reported sizes across the new quantization options:

UD-IQ1_S: 6.2GB
UD-IQ1_M: 6.7GB
UD-IQ2_S: 8.4GB
UD-Q3_K_XL: 13.1GB
UD-IQ4_XS: 14.3GB
UD-Q4_K_M: 16.5GB
UD-Q6_K: 22GB

The smallest version is particularly interesting for people working with limited RAM or VRAM. But file size alone doesn’t tell you how well a model will perform.

The real challenge is compressing the weights without losing too much capability.

Quantization stores model weights at lower numerical precision, reducing the memory required to load them. The trade-off is that aggressive compression can affect reasoning, coding, instruction following, and output consistency.

Unsloth’s Dynamic 3.0 approach aims to preserve more of the original model’s behaviour at a given size. Its practical value depends on how well that claim holds up across independent evaluations and different tasks.

The new files contain the updated quantization. You can’t convert an older GGUF into Dynamic 3.0 simply by changing a setting in LM Studio or adding a command-line option to llama.cpp.

Compatibility is another important detail.

The new GGUFs are intended for compatible configurations using:

llama.cpp
LM Studio
NVIDIA GPUs through CUDA-compatible builds
AMD GPUs, including Strix Halo, with compatible llama.cpp builds
CPU inference
Apple Silicon through llama.cpp and Metal

According to the supplied announcement, native MLX versions are not available yet.

There is also a difference between Dynamic 3.0 and MTP.

Dynamic 3.0 focuses on the memory-versus-quality trade-off. MTP, or Multi-Token Prediction, can help accelerate generation through compatible speculative decoding implementations.

One targets how efficiently the model is stored. The other targets how efficiently it generates tokens.

The 6.2GB UD-IQ1_S file is the headline number, but the smallest quant isn’t necessarily the right choice for every workload. Lower precision can introduce quality losses, and inference also requires memory for the runtime, context, KV cache, and other overhead.

A 6.2GB model file does not mean the entire workload will fit comfortably into 8GB of RAM or VRAM.

For local AI users, the useful question is how much capability each quant retains, how fast it runs, and how much memory remains available for longer contexts.

If Dynamic 3.0 delivers on its quality-preservation goal, it could give more people practical access to Qwen3.8-27B without requiring a hardware upgrade.

1973年10月17日爆发的第一次石油危机是全球地缘政治、国际货币体系与全球化分工底层逻辑的一次大洗牌。

在这天，石油输出国组织（OPEC）中的阿拉伯成员国（OAPEC）宣布逐月减产5%，并对支持以色列的西方国家实施严厉的石油禁运。这一举动，直接将原油价格在短短几个月内从每桶不到3美元飙升至近12美元，涨幅接近400%。

要真正理解这场危机的深远影响，我们需要从以下三个极具深度的底层维度进行穿透式剖析：

一、 经济底层的重塑：滞胀的诞生与凯恩斯主义的破产

在1973年之前，西方主流经济学信奉凯恩斯主义，认为“高通胀”和“高失业率（经济停滞）”如同硬币的两面，不可能同时出现。然而，石油危机用一种极为粗暴的方式颠覆了这一理论。

供给侧冲击（Supply Shock）的威力：过去，经济危机多由需求不足引起。而石油作为工业的“血液”，其价格暴涨直接导致全球商品和服务的生产成本急剧飙升。企业在成本重压下不得不裁员、减产，引发了前所未有的“滞胀”（Stagflation）现象。

倒逼产业结构向“轻量化”转型：这场危机终结了西方战后长达20年的“汽车黄金时代”。美国底特律那些排量大、油耗高的“肌肉车”遭遇灭顶之灾，而主打省油、经济的日本小型汽车则借此机会彻底攻占了美国和全球市场，全球制造业开始向低能耗、精细化方向转型。

二、 金融帝国的重组：美元-石油”霸权体系的奠定

1971年，美国总统尼克松宣布美元与黄金脱钩，导致布雷顿森林体系瓦解，美元信用面临崩溃。然而，1973年的石油危机却极其诡异地为美国提供了一个修复美元霸权的绝佳历史契机。

石油美元（Petrodollar）的闭环构建：油价暴涨4倍后，全球对美元的需求不仅没有减少，反而因为“买石油必须用美元”而呈现指数级增长。1974年，美国与沙特阿拉伯达成秘密协议：沙特确保其石油只用美元结算，而美国则向沙特提供军事保护。

财富重分配的金融回流：中东产油国通过高油价赚取了海量的美元（被称为“石油美元”）。这些资金无法在当地完全消化，只能源源不断地重新存入华尔街的银行，或者购买美国国债。至此，美元成功完成了从“锚定黄金”向“锚定石油”的惊天跃升，牢牢卡住了全球经济的命门。

三、 地缘政治的转向：西方分化与能源安全概念的诞生

在这场危机中，面对阿拉伯世界的石油武器，西方阵营内部表现出了极大的撕裂和恐慌。

大国阵营的分化：严重依赖中东石油的西欧和日本，在外交政策上迅速与美国拉开距离，开始倾向于亲阿拉伯的立场，以换取石油供应。这表明在极限生存资源面前，“盟友关系”必须让位于“能源安全”。

国家战略储备与替代能源的崛起：这场危机催生了现代意义上的“国家战略石油储备（SPR）”制度。同时，西方各国开始疯狂寻找替代能源：法国在此后举国体制发展核电，使其至今仍是全球核电占比最高的国家；巴西开始大力研发生物乙醇燃料；全球对太阳能、风能等新能源的早期探索也正是从此时期被迫启航。

历史的镜鉴：从1973看2026

1973年的石油危机告诉我们：任何一种核心资源的绝对垄断，在特定地缘政治周期下，都会被必然地武器化。
跨越半个世纪，当我们站在2026年的节点审视当下，全球正在上演极其相似的剧本，只是核心资源从当年的“石油”变成了今天的“AI高级算力、半导体先进工艺、以及稀有关键金属（如镓、锗、锂）”。历史没有重复，但押着相同的韵脚。从1973年的“能源脱钩”到当今的“技术脱钩”，大国博弈的底层逻辑依然是夺取全球核心要素的定价权。

TITLE
AI News: China Proposes AI Export Controls, US Oversight Review, Research Access
https://t.co/4oEHZdlocz

DESCRIPTION
China proposes AI export controls as global developments span AI oversight, education, healthcare, forecasting and scientific research.

AI-generation disclosure: This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

Chapters
00:00 China proposes AI export controls
00:32 White House starts AI oversight review
00:57 Japan union requests AI voice consent

SOURCES

https://t.co/v3NhCUW65u — Mistral AI on GitHub
https://t.co/JGJF6Xtp7p — Simons Foundation
https://t.co/MQsqcFSqDw — OpenAI

https://t.co/rEbrg5gzyl — Tohoku University
https://t.co/5Zx0MDAA6x — Solafune
https://t.co/WvI5fVzKZB — Hong Kong Productivity Council (HKPC) / FLAIR
https://t.co/8B0J1bHf5p — Media OutReach Newswire (syndicated by Vietnam News)
https://t.co/9wooSX97Y5 — South Korea Ministry of Science and ICT
https://t.co/PHfnlFZbMc — Bertis
https://t.co/k7VtKKCSgH — Bertis

TRANSCRIPT
Transferring advanced Chinese AI technology abroad could face new limits. China proposes adding 23 AI technologies to its export-control catalog, including large models, agents and computing clusters. Covered transfers already require interim pre-export registration, while the catalog changes remain under consultation through November 15. Public-domain technology is excluded, and the ministry says ordinary model access through apps or online interfaces falls outside the described model-technology export scope.

Federal oversight of AI could change how developers handle cybersecurity, biological risks and consumer protection. After adopting its charter, the White House task force commissioned a scientific-advisory report on those risks and model accountability. That starts a 120-day oversight review, with working groups addressing cyber-breach reporting and consumer protection. This is a review and coordination process, with no new binding rule announced.

Performers face AI systems that can train on and recreate their voices. Japan Actors Union asks developers and users to obtain prior permission, state the purpose and agree fair compensation. Its new voluntary guidance covers training, voice generation and publication or other use, including deceased performers and dubbing. The union describes a gap in comprehensive voice protection, but its guidance does not create a new law.

Independent scrutiny of major AI systems and protections for children are the focus of a new advocacy platform. Humans First calls for mandatory independent testing, public AI-incident reporting and liability for frontier developers’ reckless conduct. The group also wants strict rules for AI used by children and urges Congress to act. These are policy demands reported by Semafor, without governmental adoption or a reported legislative sponsor.

Serious AI incidents could create risks across national borders, making communication between major AI powers consequential. The South China Morning Post, citing unnamed sources, reports regular American and Chinese technical-team talks on details of an AI-incident channel and bilateral dialogue. The discussions follow the earlier channel commitment. Sources hope cooperation could feature at the expected November leaders’ meeting, but the report establishes no finalized agreement or functioning mechanism.

Portuguese-speaking teachers have a new route to practical training on AI classroom tasks. OpenAI’s AI for Educators course covers lesson planning, activities, assessments and school communications, while keeping pedagogical judgment with educators. The free OpenAI Academy course is now available in Brazilian Portuguese for primary, secondary and higher-education educators. The announcement establishes access to training, without demonstrating better student outcomes.

University research labs can face costs when accessing specialized AI tools for life sciences. OpenAI’s Rosalind Academic Plan offers eligible American university labs sponsored access to its life-sciences research model, supporting literature review, research-data work and scientific tools. Approved labs can receive up to 30 complimentary ChatGPT Business Standard seats for up to twelve months, with Rosalind subject to trusted-access approval. The offer excludes programmatic API access and establishes no scientific or clinical result.

Complex hospital workflows and fragmented reporting can require substantial manual effort. UMass Memorial says Accenture will introduce AI agents to automate complex workflows and uncover insights, alongside a Microsoft Azure data-platform modernization. The multiyear initiative is intended to help clinicians access insights more efficiently. It remains an announced plan, with no completed deployment, clinical outcome or cost result reported.

Planning energy supply, maintenance and capacity depends on anticipating changes in data. Mistral’s Timestral AI family generates probabilistic forecasts across related data streams and can incorporate known future inputs, such as weather forecasts and production schedules. The released models range from five million to 209 million parameters. Mistral says they run without graphics processors and reports leading benchmark results, which do not establish customer savings or production outcomes.

Mathematicians need ways to scrutinize AI-assisted results and agree how these tools should be used. Simons Foundation, Anthropic and OpenAI are committing fifteen million dollars in combined funding and resources for evaluation, tool learning and collective standards. Simons will manage awards, including an open call, while the companies plan to provide tools and computing resources. OpenAI’s five-million-dollar contribution is included in the package, and the initiative does not certify AI mathematics as correct.

CERN expects much larger collision datasets, increasing the challenge of extracting scientific findings. It and Mistral plan a foundation model trained on billions of simulated particle collisions, intended to reconstruct events, identify particles and flag unexpected signals. A signed statement of intent starts the partnership, with detector-design evaluation also envisaged. This is a development plan without announced performance results, budget or timetable.

More useful satellite observations could support environmental monitoring, resource management and disaster prevention. Tohoku University and Solafune plan onboard AI that analyzes and integrates data, then feeds results back into later observation planning. The partners aim to build, launch and demonstrate the concept in orbit. Their research combines satellite engineering with AI imagery analysis; no operating service or measured monitoring benefit is reported.

AI-enabled robots need testing beyond laboratories before businesses can judge their usefulness at work. Hong Kong’s Productivity Council has opened a hub through FLAIR for embodied-AI model training, adaptation, evaluation and iteration in real settings. Its first phase gathers seven technology partners and eight scenario partners across manufacturing, logistics, retail, inspection and public services. The announcement describes testing infrastructure, without established mass deployment or measured productivity gains.

Manufacturers, startups and smaller firms could gain more coordinated support for adopting AI. South Korea’s science, industry and small-business ministries announced a planned agreement spanning core AI capabilities, commercialization research and regional industrial ecosystems. A manufacturing task force is also planned. The release gives no funding total, rollout schedule or measured adoption result, and announces scheduled signing rather than confirming completed execution.

Choosing useful drug targets is an early challenge in developing possible treatments. Bertis says its SURF platform combines protein analysis with AI to discover, prioritize and validate cell-surface protein targets. The company says government research funding will provide three billion won over three years to advance the platform. That funds research, with no newly validated target, clinical result or approved medicine reported.

Subscribe to stay updated every eight hours on AI developments worldwide.

ANNALS OF THE DAY 🪔

══════════════ ❧ ══════════════

A Historical Chronicle: October 17 Edition

────────────── ◈ ──────────────

EPIGRAPH

“We carry yesterday like a lantern—not to live in its light, but to see how far we’ve already come, and how much farther we need to go.” ~ Hodgepodgery, 2026

────────────── ◈ ──────────────

INTRO

Today we reflect on pivotal military capitulations, industrial disasters, groundbreaking scientific developments, and legendary cultural and athletic milestones. From the decisive surrender at Saratoga and the sudden devastation of the London Beer Flood to major shifts in global energy geopolitics, iconic comic strip debuts, and memorable World Series clashes, October 17 showcases the immense breadth of human history.

────────────────────────────────

🧭 CALENDAR OVERVIEW

October 17 is the 290th day of the year in the Gregorian calendar (≈79.45% of the year completed). There are 75 days remaining after this date, representing (≈20.55%) of the year. The year 2026 is a common year (365 days). Today is Saturday, falling in ISO week 42. Verified observances for this date include International Day for the Eradication of Poverty, National Edge Day, and Black Poetry Day.

────────────────────────────────

🏛️ MAJOR HISTORICAL EVENTS

Major historical events on this date reflect turning points in diplomacy, wartime conflict, industrial disasters, and civic movements.

1346 — Battle of Neville’s Cross

On Monday, October 17, 1346, King David II of Scotland invaded northern England in support of France and was defeated near Durham by forces under Ralph Neville. Wounded and captured, he spent the next eleven years as an English prisoner while his nephew Robert Stewart governed Scotland, until his release under the Treaty of Berwick in 1357.

🧩 TRIVIA: Contemporary accounts and later tradition hold that David II was found hiding under a bridge over the River Browney after the battle; during his capture he reportedly knocked out two of his captor’s teeth.

🌀 OBSCURE: Although Edward III was campaigning in France at the time, David was first held in the Tower of London before being moved among other English castles, including Odiham, until his ransom of 100,000 marks was agreed.

1777 — British General John Burgoyne Surrenders at Saratoga

On Friday, October 17, 1777, British Major General John Burgoyne surrendered his army of over 5,000 men to American forces under Major General Horatio Gates at Saratoga, New York. Burgoyne’s attempt to march south from Canada and isolate New England collapsed after logistical failures, difficult terrain, and defeats at the Battles of Saratoga left his force surrounded and cut off. The American victory became the turning point of the Revolutionary War, convincing France to enter the conflict as a formal American ally.

🧩 TRIVIA: The surrender document was officially titled a Convention rather than a Capitulation because Burgoyne insisted on negotiated terms that would allow his troops to march out with full military honors.

⚠️ IRONYѰ: Burgoyne had famously boasted in London society before departing that he would return victorious within a single campaign season without losing a single regiment.

1814 — The London Beer Flood Engulfs St. Giles

On Monday, October 17, 1814, a giant wooden vat of fermenting porter ruptured at the Meux and Company Brewery on Tottenham Court Road, triggering a chain reaction that released a tidal wave of more than 320,000 gallons of beer into the streets of St. Giles. The flood destroyed two houses, collapsed a tenement building, and killed eight people—mostly women and children trapped in basement dwellings.

🧩 TRIVIA: Parliament eventually granted Meux and Company a tax refund on the lost excise duty paid for the destroyed beer, saving the firm from total financial ruin.

❓ DID YOU KNOW‽: The brewery stood trial for the disaster in a civil court, but the jury ruled the incident to be an Act of God, leaving the victims' families without financial compensation.

1931 — Al Capone Convicted of Federal Income Tax Evasion

On Saturday, October 17, 1931, Chicago crime boss Al Capone was convicted in federal court on five counts of income tax evasion.

🧩 TRIVIA: Judge James Herbert Wilkerson secretly swapped the entire jury pool right before the trial began after federal agents discovered Capone's associates had bribed the original panel.

🔑 ESOTERIC: The legal foundation for Capone's prosecution rested on the 1927 United States Supreme Court ruling United States v. Sullivan, which established that illegal gains are fully subject to federal income tax laws and that claiming Fifth Amendment protections does not exempt a citizen from filing a return.

1933 — Albert Einstein Arrives in the United States as a Refugee

Renowned theoretical physicist Albert Einstein arrived in New York City fleeing Nazi persecution in Germany, establishing his new permanent residence at the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton.

🧩 TRIVIA: Einstein officially renounced his German citizenship while visiting the German consulate in Antwerp earlier that same year.

❓ DID YOU KNOW‽: His arrival marked a major migration of European intellectuals to American academic institutions during the interwar era, permanently transforming the landscape of modern scientific research.

1973 — OAPEC Establishes the First Arab Oil Embargo

On October 17, 1973, Arab members of the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, led by Saudi Arabia, proclaimed a selective oil embargo against nations that supported Israel during the Yom Kippur War. Target nations included the United States, Great Britain, Canada, Japan, and the Netherlands. Coupled with immediate production cuts, the embargo choked global energy supplies, sending crude oil prices soaring from three dollars per barrel to nearly twelve dollars worldwide. The embargo triggered severe stagflation across Western economies, leading to widespread gas shortages, rationing, speed limit reductions, and profound changes in international energy policy.

🧩 TRIVIA: Oregon became the first U.S. state to implement an odd-even license plate gasoline rationing system during the crisis to shorten long lines at pumps.

🌪️ TWIST: While designed as a political punishment, the sudden spike in prices allowed non-Arab oil producers, including the Soviet Union, to generate unprecedented revenue booms that temporarily bolstered their domestic economies.

1979 — Mother Teresa Awarded the Nobel Peace Prize

Albanian-Indian Catholic nun Mother Teresa was announced as the recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for her work with the poor in Calcutta, requesting that the traditional ceremonial banquet be canceled.

🧩 TRIVIA: The banquet budget of roughly $192,000 was converted directly into meals that fed over 15,000 people in need.

🏆 FIRST: She was the first Albanian-born recipient of the prestigious peace award, cementing her status as a global symbol of charitable devotion.

1989 — Loma Prieta Earthquake Strikes Northern California

A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the San Francisco Bay Area during a live broadcast of the Major League Baseball World Series, causing 63 deaths and catastrophic damage to regional infrastructure.

🧩 TRIVIA: It was the first major earthquake along the San Andreas fault zone to be captured live on international television due to pre-game sports coverage.

🌀 OBSCURE: The earthquake temporarily disrupted the 1989 World Series between the Oakland Athletics and San Francisco Giants, leading to a ten-day delay before play resumed.

2003 — The Taipei 101 Skyscraper Reaches Its Structural Pinnacle

Construction crews in Taiwan placed the final structural spire on Taipei 101, officially making it the tallest building in the world at 508 meters (1,667 feet).

🧩 TRIVIA: The tower features a massive 660-tonne tuned mass damper suspended inside its top floors to stabilize the structure against typhoons and earthquakes.

❓ DID YOU KNOW‽: Its architectural design draws heavy inspiration from traditional Asian pagoda structures, utilizing repetitive modular sections structured like rising bamboo shoots.

2011 — Occupy Wall Street Protests Expand Globally

Following the movement’s launch in Zuccotti Park, New York, a coordinated global day of action on October 15 saw Occupy-inspired demonstrations spread across more than 900 cities, protesting corporate influence and wealth inequality. Coverage and further actions continued into the following days.

🧩 TRIVIA: The famous “We are the 99%” slogan was originally coined in August 2011 on a Tumblr blog prior to the initial New York encampments.

🌪️ TWIST: The decentralized nature of the movement allowed it to spread rapidly worldwide, though it ultimately struggled to achieve concrete legislative reforms due to its lack of centralized leadership.

These pivotal events continue to shape the course of history.   🌍

────────────────────────────────

🔬 SCIENTIFIC, TECHNOLOGICAL, AND CULTURAL MILESTONES

Scientific and cultural breakthroughs on this day brought historic postal routes, beloved cartoon debuts, legendary chess masterworks, and landmark horror literature.

1558 — Establishment of Poczta Polska

On Saturday, October 18, 1558, King Sigismund II Augustus established a permanent postal route between Kraków and Venice, marking the official birth of the Polish postal system. (The date is traditionally observed on the 18th.)

🧩 TRIVIA: The royal postal route was created primarily to maintain secure personal correspondence between the Polish court and Italian diplomats. Fixed royal courier relays along the Trans-European Alpine corridors instituted a standardized post-house system that reduced mail delivery times across Central Europe from months to mere weeks.

🔑 ESOTERIC: The establishment of fixed royal courier relays along the Trans-European Alpine corridors instituted a standardized post-house system that reduced mail delivery times across Central Europe from months to mere weeks.
1937 — Huey, Dewey, and Louie Debut in Newspaper Comics

The three mischief-making nephews of Donald Duck appeared for the first time in a nationally syndicated newspaper comic strip illustrated by Al Taliaferro.

🧩 TRIVIA: The nephews were originally created to deliver a letter of introduction to Donald from their mother, Della Duck.

❓ DID YOU KNOW‽: Their iconic colored outfits—red for Huey, blue for Dewey, and green for Louie—were later popularized by Carl Barks in comic book adaptations to help readers distinguish the identical triplets.

1956 — Bobby Fischer Wins the "Game of the Century"

Thirteen-year-old chess prodigy Bobby Fischer defeated Donald Byrne at the Marshall Chess Club in New York City, executing an extraordinary queen sacrifice.

🧩 TRIVIA: International Grandmaster Hans Kmoch declared the game a masterpiece of tactical combination that would be studied for centuries.

🌪️ TWIST: Despite playing with the black pieces against an experienced master, Fischer launched a breathtaking series of tactical maneuvers that left his opponent's king completely defenseless across the board.

1975 — Stephen King Publishes 'Salem's Lot

Doubleday released Stephen King's second published novel, 'Salem's Lot, cementing his position as a preeminent master of modern horror literature.

🧩 TRIVIA: King originally wanted to title the book Second Coming, but his wife Tabitha pointed out that it sounded more like a religious text than a vampire tale.

🌀 OBSCURE: The fictional town of Jerusalem's Lot was heavily inspired by the small-town isolation King experienced while growing up in rural Maine.

1979 — Creation of the United States Department of Education

President Jimmy Carter signed the Department of Education Organization Act into law, splitting federal educational policy from the former Department of Health, Education, and Welfare.

🧩 TRIVIA: The cabinet-level agency officially began operations on May 4, 1980, with Shirley Hufstedler serving as its inaugural secretary.

🏆 FIRST: This marked the formal establishment of education as an independent cabinet-level department within the United States federal government.

A day of enduring breakthroughs in how we connect, imagine, and organize.  ✨

────────────────────────────────

🎂 FAMOUS BIRTHDAYS

Warmest birthday wishes and fond remembrances to these celebrated figures in literature, science, public service, and the arts!

1912 — Pope John Paul I

Italian head of the Catholic Church who served a brief 33-day pontificate in 1978. Born in Forno di Canale, Italy.

🧩 TRIVIA: He was the first pope in Catholic history to adopt a dual papal name, honoring both of his immediate predecessors, John XXIII and Paul VI.

1914 — Jerry Siegel

American comic book writer and co-creator of Superman alongside artist Joe Shuster. Born in Cleveland, Ohio.

🧩 TRIVIA: Siegel worked as a clerk and delivery boy while writing the initial scripts for Action Comics No. 1 in the late 1930s.

1918 — Rita Hayworth

American actress and dancer who achieved international fame during Hollywood's Golden Age. Born in Brooklyn, New York.

🧩 TRIVIA: Before taking her screen name, she performed professionally as a dancer under her birth name, Margarita Carmen Cansino.

1920 — Montgomery Clift

Four-time Academy Award-nominated American actor famous for his intense method acting style. Born in Omaha, Nebraska.

🧩 TRIVIA: Clift was one of the earliest Hollywood stars invited to join the Actors Studio alongside Marlon Brando.

1938 — Evel Knievel

American stunt performer and daredevil famed for his long-distance motorcycle jumps. Born in Butte, Montana.

🧩 TRIVIA: He selected his famous moniker "Evel" after spending a night in jail next to a local criminal nicknamed "Awful" Knofel.

1942 — Jim Seals

American singer, songwriter, and multi-instrumentalist best known as one half of the soft-rock duo Seals & Crofts. Born in Sidney, Texas.

🧩 TRIVIA: Seals was a multi-instrumentalist who won a Texas state fiddle championship as a child, later played saxophone with the Champs (of “Tequila” fame), and co-wrote the duo’s signature hits “Summer Breeze” (1972) and “Diamond Girl” (1973), both of which reached No. 6 on the Billboard Hot 100.

🧬 HUMAN ANGLE: A longtime adherent of the Baháʼí Faith, he lived for years on a coffee plantation in Costa Rica after the duo’s initial breakup and was the older brother of country-pop singer Dan Seals (of England Dan & John Ford Coley).

1947 — Michael McKean (age 79)

American actor and musician best known for portraying David St. Hubbins in This Is Spinal Tap and Lenny Kosnowski on Laverne & Shirley. Born in New York City, New York.

🧩 TRIVIA: McKean served as a musical performer and regular cast member on Saturday Night Live during the mid-1990s.

1948 — George Wendt

American actor and comedian best known for his iconic portrayal of Norm Peterson on the long-running sitcom Cheers. Born in Chicago, Illinois.

🧩 TRIVIA: Wendt studied economics at Notre Dame before joining The Second City comedy troupe in Chicago during the late 1970s.

1956 — Mae Jemison (age 70)

American engineer and physician who became the first Black woman to travel into space aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour. Born in Decatur, Alabama.

🧩 TRIVIA: Before joining NASA, Dr. Jemison served as a Peace Corps medical officer in Sierra Leone and Liberia.

1958 — Alan Jackson (age 68)

Country music icon who authored dozens of hit singles blending traditional neotraditional country with modern storytelling. Born in Newnan, Georgia. 

🧩 TRIVIA: Jackson wrote his breakout hit "Here in the Real World" while working in the mailroom of The Nashville Network.

1962 — Mike Judge (age 64)

Animator and filmmaker who created iconic animated series including Beavis and Butt-Head and King of the Hill. Born in Guayaquil, Ecuador.

🧩 TRIVIA: Judge earned a degree in physics from UC San Diego and worked as a test engineer before entering the animation industry.

1972 — Eminem (age 54)

Grammy-winning rapper, songwriter, and record producer recognized as one of the most influential artists in hip-hop history. Born in Saint Joseph, Missouri.

🧩 TRIVIA: He competed under the stage name "M&M" during high school freestyle battles before changing the spelling to Eminem.

1979 — Kimi Räikkönen (age 47)

Finnish Formula One driver who won the 2007 World Drivers' Championship driving for Scuderia Ferrari. Born in Espoo, Finland.

🧩 TRIVIA: Nicknamed "The Iceman," he holds the record for the highest number of Grand Prix starts between 2001 and 2021. Happy birthday to them all!

Happy birthday to them all!  🎉

────────────────────────────────

🥀 MEMORIAM

A heartfelt tribute and solemn remembrance to the legends, visionaries, and public servants who shaped our world and left behind an unforgettable mark.

1849 — Frédéric Chopin (aged 39)

The Polish master composer and virtuoso pianist whose nocturnes and mazurkas redefined solo piano composition died in Paris, France, following a long battle with chronic pulmonary tuberculosis.

🧩 TRIVIA: In accordance with his deathbed wish, his heart was removed post-mortem and transported secretly back to Poland, where it remains enshrined in Warsaw.

🌀 OBSCURE: Chopin's funeral at the Church of the Madeleine in Paris featured the performance of Mozart's Requiem, a piece he had specifically requested during his final days.

1868 — Laura Secord (aged 93)

The Canadian War of 1812 heroine famous for walking roughly 20 miles through dangerous territory to warn British forces of an American ambush died peacefully in Chippawa, Ontario.

🧩 TRIVIA: Her heroic trek went largely unacknowledged by the government until she was awarded a grant by the Prince of Wales at age 85.

🧬 HUMAN ANGLE: Despite her grueling physical journey and vital intelligence contribution, Secord lived much of her life in relative obscurity running a small schoolhouse.

1937 — J. Bruce Ismay (aged 74)

The English businessman and chairman of the White Star Line who survived the 1912 sinking of the RMS Titanic died of a stroke in London, England, after spending his final decades in quiet seclusion.

🧩 TRIVIA: Ismay personally financed maritime charities and established a fund for British merchant seamen after leaving corporate leadership.

🌪️ TWIST: The intense public backlash and media scrutiny surrounding his survival of the disaster haunted him for the rest of his life, causing him to withdraw almost entirely from public society.

1965 — Bart King (aged 92)

The legendary American cricketer, widely regarded as one of the greatest swing bowlers in the history of the sport, died in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania.

🧩 TRIVIA: King developed his unique bowling delivery by experimenting with curved pitches while playing baseball during his youth.

🌀 OBSCURE: He toured England multiple times with the Philadelphia cricket team, dominating top-tier international batsmen with his exceptional bowling mastery.
text

1967 — Puyi (aged 61)

The last Emperor of China and final ruler of the Qing Dynasty died of kidney cancer in Beijing, China, after a life that took him from the imperial throne through Japanese puppet rule, Soviet captivity, and Communist re-education to a final role as a modest gardener and civilian researcher.

🧩 TRIVIA: His autobiography, From Emperor to Citizen, was used as the primary source material for Bernardo Bertolucci's Oscar-winning film The Last Emperor.

❓ DID YOU KNOW‽: Puyi lived through the fall of the empire, Japanese puppet rule in Manchukuo, Soviet captivity, and Chinese Communist re-education before his final years as a civilian researcher.
text

1979 — S.J. Perelman (Sidney Joseph Perelman) (aged 75)

The American humorist and Oscar-winning screenwriter celebrated for his satirical essays in The New Yorker and his comedic screenplays for the Marx Brothers died of natural causes in New York City.

🧩 TRIVIA: Perelman co-wrote the screenplay for the 1956 film Around the World in 80 Days, winning an Academy Award for Best Adapted Screenplay.

🌀 OBSCURE: Known for his elaborate vocabulary and deadpan surrealism, Perelman was described by contemporaries as one of the most brilliant prose stylists of the 20th century.

1991 — Tennessee Ernie Ford (Ernest Jennings Ford) (aged 72)

The American singer and television host who earned international acclaim for his deep baritone recording of the coal-miner song “Sixteen Tons” died of liver failure in Reston, Virginia.

🧩 TRIVIA: Ford served as a bombardier on a B-29 Superfortress during World War II prior to launching his country and gospel music career.

🏆 FIRST: His crossover recording of “Sixteen Tons” broke sales records in 1955, remaining at the top of the country charts for ten consecutive weeks.

2007 — Joey Bishop (aged 89)

The American comedian and actor who served as a core member of the “Rat Pack” alongside Frank Sinatra, Dean Martin, Sammy Davis Jr., and Peter Lawford died of heart failure in Newport Beach, California.

🧩 TRIVIA: Bishop was the long-running host of his own late-night talk show, The Joey Bishop Show, which aired on NBC and ABC in the 1960s.

🧬 HUMAN ANGLE: Known for his dry, self-deprecating wit, Bishop was frequently credited by his peers as the sharpest improvisational jokester among the legendary Rat Pack performers.

In fond remembrance of them all.  🕯️

────────────────────────────────

🏟️ SPORTS HIGHLIGHTS

On this day, historic championships and athletic milestones captivated sports fans around the world.

1860 — First British Open Championship Held at Prestwick

The inaugural Open Championship was played at Prestwick Golf Club in Ayrshire, Scotland, with eight professional golfers competing over three rounds.

🧩 TRIVIA: Willie Park Sr. won the first tournament by two strokes, earning the Challenge Belt made of red leather with silver buckles.

🏆 FIRST: This marked the birth of modern professional major golf championships.

1978 — New York Yankees Win World Series Game 6

The New York Yankees defeated the Los Angeles Dodgers 7-2 in Game 6 to secure their second consecutive World Series championship title.

🧩 TRIVIA: Boston became the first team in Major League Baseball history to overcome a 3-0 series deficit and advance to the World Series.

AI Field Notes #120

AI reviewers found so many defects in PostgreSQL 19 that 8 to 10 features got pulled and the release slipped to about Nov 19.

- GitHub Copilot now fixes up to 25 security alerts in one draft pull request
- Claude spent 53 hours redesigning quantum circuits, up to 17x fewer gates
- OpenAI's rogue-agent log hits 19; India's CERT-In says lab agents read confidential data
- Replit says it dropped Anthropic over cost and performance
- Accenture caps staff Claude spend at $29 a month

TODAY'S STORIES:

1. PostgreSQL 19 slips a month as AI-assisted review helps push out 8 to 10 features
Backend engineers who planned a Postgres 19 upgrade for graph queries should plan for version 20 instead. Any maintainer can take the lesson: point an LLM reviewer at old code and budget real weeks for the backlog it produces.

2. GitHub Agentic Autofix: Copilot now fixes up to 25 security alerts in one pull request
An application security engineer's week shifts from writing fixes to reviewing an agent's pull requests. Check the meter before assigning 25 alerts at once, since credits and Actions minutes both count.

3. NIST curve seeds: Claude traces a 1990s crypto mystery to a C library RNG in 30 minutes
Nothing in your TLS setup needs to change. Security engineers should note the method: a model spotted a bit pattern humans missed for decades, so the 'random' constants in your own code deserve a second look.

4. Rogue AI agents: OpenAI logs 19 incidents as India's CERT-In reports data exposure
Any API key sitting in a public repo or an over-permissive cloud role is now reachable by test agents from labs you have never dealt with. A DevOps engineer should rotate those keys this week and treat evaluation traffic as untrusted traffic.

5. METR inside Anthropic: six outside researchers get staff access and publication rights
Engineers building on Claude get a second opinion on the risk reports that shape its usage rules, written by people who saw the internals. Read the first one for what was redacted as much as for what was said.

6. FLUX 3 Klein: Black Forest Labs opens a 5.6B image model that runs on an 8GB GPU
A freelance designer can now run editing and multi-reference generation locally without sending client photos to a cloud API. Agencies past $5 million in revenue need a paid license, so read it before building a pipeline on it.

7. Proofpoint buys Varonis for $6.3B to watch what AI agents touch in company data
IT admins who already run Varonis should expect it to fold into the Proofpoint suite, with new pricing to match. The permissions your staff never cleaned up are the permissions your agents will use.

8. App Store rules: Apple bans nudify apps that hide their purpose from review
Indie developers shipping image-generation features need visible safeguards and a moderation plan before their next review. Parents get a slightly cleaner App Store, though the web versions of these apps stay one link away.

9. Amazon Bee: $75 and $100 AI wearables that record and summarize your conversations
Therapists and managers should expect more meetings where someone's wrist is taking notes. If you wear one, check your state's recording-consent rules before you switch it on at work.

ONE STORY THAT MOVES THE FLOOR:

The application security engineer at a GitHub Enterprise shop starts Monday with a queue of CodeQL alerts. Since October 15 she can select 25 at once and assign them to Copilot, which writes the fixes, reruns the scan and opens a draft pull request. Her week is now reviewing an agent's work. Who on your team still writes the security fix by hand?

SEOUL NOW PRICES SK HYNIX $SKHY AS IF THIS IS THE BEST YEAR IT WILL EVER HAVE:

SK Hynix (SKHY) at $136.49, -$9.62 / -6.58% on Friday.

That price is for its US-traded shares, which trade after Seoul closes. At home, SK Hynix lost 24.3% this week and Samsung Electronics (005930 in Seoul) 17.8%, each its worst week since October 2008, Benzinga reported.

The verdict: this was not a vote against Korea. It was a bet that the memory-chip boom is at or near its peak. SK Hynix now sells for under four times its current operating profit, a price investors pay only for profits they expect to shrink. The first real test of that bet is its own July-September report, Tuesday, October 27, at 8pm ET.

Nothing in Asia trades until Sunday at 8pm ET, when Seoul and Tokyo open together at 9am Monday local time. Friday's closes, from Thursday:

- Kospi (South Korea): 5,668.05, +113.83 points / +2.05%.
- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 65,324, +898 points / +1.39%.
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 24,187, +124 points / +0.52%.
- Shanghai Composite: 3,716.28, +8.80 points / +0.24%.

Friday hides the week. From the last close before it (arithmetic):

- Seoul: -14.46%.
- Tokyo: -5.4%.
- Shanghai: -2.6%.
- Hong Kong: -0.1%.

The more a market leans on chipmakers, the harder it fell, and Seoul's index leans hardest. Its slide ran seven sessions through Thursday for a 20.7% loss (arithmetic). Thursday alone took 7.57%, after a drop of more than 8% during the day set off a 20-minute halt to all trading. Foreign investors sold nine sessions straight, roughly 18 trillion won this month, about $13 billion, then turned buyers Friday.

Three blows landed in one week:

- Saturday, October 10: Cao Kanyu, president of China's largest memory maker, CXMT (688825 in Shanghai), said it will launch server memory by the end of 2026 on a denser design, 4F2, that fits about 50% more memory cells on a chip. SK Hynix fell 10.09% in Seoul on Tuesday.
- Wednesday, October 14: September consumer prices, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics, +3.7% from a year earlier vs 3.6% expected, lifting the odds of another Fed rate increase.
- All week: worry over how US AI companies keep borrowing to build data centers.

The strongest case against the selling is the business. SK Hynix's April-June quarter, from its own filing:

- Revenue, the money coming in the door: 79.3 trillion won, +257% from a year earlier.
- Operating profit, what is left from making and selling chips before interest and taxes: 60.5 trillion won, about 76 won of every 100 won of sales.

That one quarter beat its operating profit for all of 2025, 47.2 trillion won. Samsung reported a record on October 8: preliminary July-September operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, the first time a Korean company has topped 100 trillion in a quarter. And CXMT has missed its own dates before: it aimed for DDR5 memory in volume by the end of 2022, and it arrived in earnest in late 2024, Korea JoongAng Daily reported.

So why the low price? SK Hynix is worth about 930 trillion won, nearly $700 billion, at Friday's Seoul close. Its April-June operating profit, run for a full year, is about 242 trillion won, so the stock costs under four times that, before tax (arithmetic). Memory is a boom-and-bust business: when supply catches up, prices fall fast. In 2023, the last bust, SK Hynix posted an operating loss of 7.7 trillion won. The cheaper it looks against this year's profit, the surer the market is that this year is the high point.

SK Hynix sits on none of the six Len5 watchlists. Deep-Value & Special-Situations hunts a sound business priced below a cautious value of its earnings, and a cautious value averages a whole memory cycle, 2023's loss included. A price that still looks cheap against that full-cycle average would put SK Hynix on the Deep-Value & Special-Situations Len5. It does pass the Quality Len5, which asks for a profitable, sound business: total liabilities, debt included, were about a third of shareholders' equity at June 30. A return to operating losses would knock it off the Quality Len5. Samsung fits none of the six for the same reason: a record quarter is the hardest profit to value cautiously.

New York traded after Seoul's Friday close and did not carry the bounce. US stock index futures, last trades before the weekend, from Thursday's settlement:

- S&P 500 futures: 7,703.00, -88.00 points / -1.13%.
- Nasdaq-100 futures: 29,391.25, -753 points / -2.50%.

One sign points away from panic: the won barely moved, near 1,340 per dollar at both ends of the week. Foreign money sold Korea's chip stocks without fleeing Korea. For US stocks, Seoul's Monday is the first live price on memory chips since Friday's selling: a Seoul close back under Thursday's 5,554.22 would say that selling carried through the weekend. Overnight moves can fade by the 9:30am ET US open.

What comes next, Eastern time:

- Sunday, 6pm: US stock index futures reopen.
- Sunday, 10pm: China's July-September GDP, two hours into Seoul's session, with Hong Kong shut for a holiday.
- Tuesday evening (Wednesday, October 21 in Seoul): Korea's October 1-20 exports, the first fresh read on chip shipments.
- Tuesday, October 27, 8pm (9am Wednesday in Seoul): SK Hynix's July-September results, a date it has confirmed. Analysts expect about 77 trillion won of operating profit, by the tally of FnGuide, a Korean financial data firm.

What would break the peak bet: operating profit near that forecast and no word of falling memory prices. What would confirm it: a margin below April-June's 76%.

The key risk: CXMT hits its date this time, and new supply arrives just as US AI buyers slow down.

A stock at under four times its profit is neither cheap nor expensive by itself. It is a forecast, and on October 27 SK Hynix gets its first chance to prove it wrong.

Not investment advice.

半导体已经连续暴跌八九天，如果接下来真的出现一轮猛烈反弹，我最看好的不是跌幅最大的AI算力云，而是存储、光模块和部分核心半导体龙头。$MU $SNDK $LITE $COHR $NVDA $AVGO

我目前重点关注六只股票，其中最看好$MU的反弹逻辑，$SNDK和$AAOI则可能拥有更大的短线弹性。

$MU：我认为是存储板块最值得关注的反弹标的。 股价从夏季高点超过1200美元回落至900美元附近，但DRAM、HBM的长期需求并没有出现同等程度的恶化。最近市场担忧长鑫存储的技术进展，但新技术距离成熟量产、良率验证和高端客户认证仍有距离。一旦韩国SK海力士止跌、市场重新交易存储供需，美光具备明显的估值修复空间。

$SNDK：弹性可能比美光更大，但风险也更高。 闪存股此前积累了巨额涨幅，近期遭到集中抛售。$SNDK主要经营NAND业务，与长鑫存储重点发展的DRAM并不相同，却同样受到整个存储板块风险偏好下降的冲击。如果市场开始重新买入存储，$SNDK可能出现猛烈反抽，但不能把超跌直接等同于低估。

$LITE、$COHR：光模块可能是另一条反弹主线。 AI数据中心继续向800G、1.6T以及更高带宽演进，光互联需求仍然存在。$LITE最新季度营收达到10.1亿美元，同比增长超过100%。市场目前主要担忧AI资本开支放缓，而不是已经确认光通信需求崩溃。如果融资担忧缓解，这两家公司有机会重新获得资金关注。

$NVDA、$AVGO：我认为它们更适合作为判断反弹质量的核心指标。 英伟达拥有GPU和CUDA生态，博通拥有定制AI芯片、高速网络以及成熟的软件现金流。真正有持续性的半导体反弹，不应该只有$AAOI、$SNDK这种高弹性股票上涨，而核心龙头依然不断创新低。

至于$AAOI，我认为它可能是反弹时涨幅非常激烈的股票之一，但并不代表它最容易形成持续上涨。客户集中度、估值和盈利兑现风险都需要考虑。

我的排序是：反弹逻辑优先看$MU、$NVDA、$AVGO；短线弹性优先看$SNDK、$LITE、$COHR，$AAOI属于更激进的选择。

但我依然维持之前的判断：10月真正的大跌风险可能还没有完全释放。

现在最需要警惕的，就是半导体突然出现一轮5%甚至10%的反弹，吸引资金重新追进去，随后再次破底。

我不会在$SOXX持续创新低的时候提前满仓赌反弹。只有韩国存储企稳、$SOXX重新跑赢$QQQ、核心半导体同步放量，才有理由提高对反弹持续性的判断。

如果只是想抓一轮超跌反弹，我会重点研究$MU和$LITE。如果准备为下一轮长期行情布局，我更倾向于$NVDA、$AVGO和$TSM。

这两种交易不能混为一谈。

跌得最狠的股票，未必是最值得买的股票。真正有价值的反弹，是基本面没有明显恶化、估值已经受到压缩，而且资金开始重新承接的公司。

A TON OF THINGS HAPPENED IN THE STOCK MARKET TODAY.

Here's a full recap:

1. The Nasdaq capped its worst week since June as the AI selloff broadened from chips into software. Per the Wall Street Journal and Investor's Business Daily via market reports, the Nasdaq Composite fell 572.99 points, or 2.14%, to 26,140.03 on Friday, the S&P 500 lost 84.62 points, or 1.09%, to 7,659.44, and the Dow fell 175.28 points, or 0.34%, to 52,002.41 after rising over 1% intraday. For the week the Nasdaq lost about 4.5% and the S&P 500 about 2%, while the Dow rose about 0.7%. Software was hit hardest Friday: the iShares Expanded Tech-Software ETF fell 4.8%, $TWLO fell 10.6% as the S&P 500's biggest decliner, $ORCL lost 5%, and $PANW and $CRWD each fell more than 7%.

2. CoreWeave became the face of AI debt fears. Reuters reported $CRWV fell more than 11% Friday, taking weekly losses to nearly 25% and putting it on track for its worst week in over 11 months, as investors focused on its roughly $50 billion debt load after hotter inflation lifted rate-hike bets and borrowing costs. Contagion hit peers: $NBIS dropped 10%, and $APLD and $IREN slipped 9% each Friday, per Reuters. Market reports added that CoreWeave's 2031 bond yield briefly passed 16% this week and five-year credit default swaps hit records above 1,000 basis points, a level described as distress, while short sellers made about $806 million on Wednesday's 15.5% drop alone, per ORTEX via Reuters.

3. Memory stocks were crushed for the week on competition fears from China. China's CXMT said it expects to launch DDR5 RDIMM server memory using a smaller 4F2 cell design around year-end, per reports cited by Reuters, raising fears the tight memory market could loosen. $MU fell 14.6% for the week, from $1,029.00 on October 9 to $878.84 on October 16, while $WDC fell 16.4% and $SNDK fell 17.9%, per AI Stock Wire's weekly tally. Elon Musk added pressure on October 15, replying to a post about a possible 2029 oversupply that China will be making a lot of RAM in 2028. Reuters noted chip stocks had already fallen for multiple sessions as investors took profits after a huge run.

4. Oil surged above $100 as supply attacks escalated. Brent settled up $3.94, or 3.72%, at $109.86 a barrel Friday after briefly touching $110, its highest since May, while WTI settled up $3.44, or 3.51%, at $101.41, its first close above $100 since September 21, per EnergyNow's settlement report. For the week WTI gained $9.56, or 10.41%, and Brent gained 4.91%. Reports cited renewed Middle East supply fears, missile attacks targeting Saudi Arabia, Ukrainian strikes on Russian refining infrastructure, a substantial U.S. crude inventory decline and continuing diesel shortages. Higher crude feeds directly into the inflation story that has kept Treasury yields above 5% and rate-hike odds elevated.

5. The Fed gave markets no relief. After hotter-than-expected CPI and PPI readings earlier in the week, Chair Kevin Warsh, speaking overnight at an IMF meeting in Bangkok, declined to signal whether the Fed would hold or hike at its October 27-28 meeting, saying in reports carried by Investopedia that it is a new chapter and the Fed is not in that business anymore. Traders cut the odds of an October hike to 17% from 28% a day earlier, but still priced an 89% chance of a December hike, per CME FedWatch. The 10-year Treasury yield held at 5.097%, the VIX jumped to 19.99, and gold settled up 0.26% at $4,181.10.

CHINA REPORTS ITS GROWTH MONDAY WITH HONG KONG SHUT. SHANGHAI TAKES THE NUMBER ALONE, JUST OFF A 14-MONTH LOW:

No stock market in Asia is trading tonight. It is Saturday morning in Tokyo. Asia's markets start reopening Sunday evening ET, Tokyo at 8pm. Two hours after that comes the biggest scheduled number of Asia's week: China's third-quarter growth figure.

The verdict: Monday's most important read in Asia comes from Shanghai, and Shanghai gets it with the main door for foreign money shut. Hong Kong is closed for a holiday, and so is Stock Connect, the main link foreign investors use to trade mainland Chinese shares. Investors inside China will set the first price on that number nearly by themselves, with their market just above its lowest close in 14 months.

Where Asia finished Friday, each from Thursday's close:

- Nikkei 225 (Japan): 65,324, +898 points / +1.39%.
- Hang Seng (Hong Kong): 24,187, +124 points / +0.52%.
- Shanghai Composite: 3,716.28, +8.81 points / +0.24%.

All three closed before New York sold off again. US stock index futures, last trades before the weekend, from Thursday's settlement:

- S&P 500 futures: 7,703.00, -88.00 points / -1.13%.
- Nasdaq-100 futures: 29,391.25, -753 points / -2.50%.
- Dow futures: 52,200, -230 points / -0.44%.

Chipmakers fell for a ninth straight day:

- iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) at $493.39, -$21.32 / -4.14% on Friday.

New York also marked down China's markets after they had closed:

- Xtrackers Harvest CSI 300 China A-Shares ETF (ASHR), which holds mainland shares, at $31.12, -$0.37 / -1.17% on Friday.
- iShares China Large-Cap ETF (FXI), which holds big Hong Kong-listed Chinese companies, at $33.84, -$0.42 / -1.23% on Friday.

Their holdings rose at home on Friday; the funds fell in New York anyway. That gap hints at a softer Monday start in Shanghai; it is a reading of the prices, not a forecast. Every fund here is a basket of stocks, so no Len5 applies.

Shanghai arrives at Monday already bruised:

- Last Friday's close: 3,813.79.
- Thursday: 3,707.48, -1.6%, its lowest close since August 15, 2025.
- The week: -2.6% (arithmetic). Reuters called it the worst week for China's stocks in three months.
- The year so far: -6.4%, and 12.4% under its May 13 closing high (arithmetic).

It closed below 3,800 on four of this week's five days. In the 12 months before this week it had done that only twice, on July 17 and July 20 (arithmetic).

Thursday's drop followed hotter US inflation, which revived bets on higher US interest rates and hit tech stocks across Asia. Lei Meng, China equity strategist at UBS Securities, said the slide looked driven by too many investors rushing out of the same tech stocks at once, while mutual funds faced withdrawals from customers who had waited to get back to even, Reuters reported. Friday's small bounce came after at least 10 AI supply-chain companies announced plans to buy back their own shares, and trading jumped late in the day in funds favored by state-backed investors, known as the "National Team," stirring talk of government support.

Monday's number, from China's National Bureau of Statistics:

- What: July-September GDP, the total output of China's economy, plus September retail sales and factory output.
- When: 10am Beijing, 30 minutes after Shanghai opens. That is 10pm ET Sunday.
- Forecast: +4.4% from a year earlier, by a Reuters poll of 50 economists, vs +4.3% in April-June.
- Beijing's 2026 goal: 4.5%-5.0%.

A 4.4% reading would be a second straight quarter under the bottom of that goal. Goldman Sachs analysts said that prospect "has increased pressure on policymakers."

The two halves of China's economy are telling different stories:

- September exports, from China's customs agency on October 14: +36.3% from a year earlier, vs 25.5% expected.
- August retail sales, what shoppers spend in stores and online: +0.4%, from the statistics bureau.
- August factory output: +5.2%.

China is selling a lot abroad while shoppers at home spend little. Monday's retail figure is the one that shows whether late-September help, targeted rate cuts and mortgage subsidies, is reaching households.

On a normal Monday, Hong Kong would give a second opinion within minutes. Its market holds China's biggest internet companies and banks, and foreign money reaches Shanghai through it. This Monday, Hong Kong's exchange lists Stock Connect closed in both directions. For one day, the only live prices for Hong Kong's big internet companies will come from New York, through US-listed shares and funds such as FXI.

For US stocks, China's number is a side issue next to this week's two big ones, AI spending and interest rates. A miss would add a third worry, weaker demand from the world's second-largest economy. A beat would not answer either of the first two. US futures reopen four hours before the release and will trade through it, and moves in that overnight session can fade by the 9:30am ET open.

What comes next, Eastern time:

- Sunday, 6pm: US stock index futures reopen.
- Sunday, 8pm: Tokyo opens, with Friday's New York selloff still to absorb.
- Sunday, 9:30pm: Shanghai opens; China's GDP lands at 10pm.
- Monday, 9:30pm: Hong Kong and Stock Connect reopen.

The level to watch is Thursday's 3,707.48 close. What would show Shanghai's selling is about China's economy, not just tech: growth under the 4.3% of April-June, and a close below that level.

The key risk: a weak figure meets a Shanghai already near a 14-month low, with Hong Kong unable to trade it until Tuesday.

Monday morning, China grades its own economy, and for one day the answer comes almost entirely from home.

Not investment advice.

A Lot Happened in the Markets Today. Here's a full recap:

1. The Nasdaq fell 4.5% this week, its biggest weekly decline since June, including a 2.15% drop on Friday. The S&P 500 lost 1.9% for the week, while the Dow gained 0.7%. The SOX semiconductor index fell for the eighth consecutive session, its longest losing streak since 2008. Brent crude rose 3.7% on Friday to $109.86 per barrel, while the VIX climbed above 20. Neocloud and memory stocks fell sharply on Friday, with CoreWeave $CRWV dropping around 12%, Nebius $NBIS losing more than 12%. Among memory stocks, Micron $MU fell 5.6% and Sandisk $SNDK dropped around 6.7%, while Western Digital $WDC, Seagate $STX and SK Hynix also finished lower.

2. Nvidia $NVDA CEO Jensen Huang said the recent selloff in AI stocks will pass. Speaking to Bloomberg in Berlin, Huang said AI is still in its early stages and that the technology will eventually transform industries around the world. He also defended the billions being spent on AI infrastructure, saying he expects those investments to generate returns despite concerns about rising borrowing costs and the recent declines in AI-related stocks.

3. SemiAnalysis reports that Nvidia $NVDA denied several neocloud providers access to GTC Berlin after they started offering AMD $AMD GPUs, TPUs and other competing chips. According to the report, executives at smaller cloud providers say Nvidia has been pressuring them to use its hardware exclusively, including networking equipment. Some executives are reportedly concerned that offering competing chips could affect their access to future Nvidia GPU allocations or the company's support for fundraising and IPOs. SemiAnalysis says larger cloud providers face less pressure because of their greater purchasing power.

4. Dell Technologies $DELL CEO Michael Dell warned that memory chip shortages could get worse in 2027 as demand from AI data centers continues to grow. Dell currently has a $95B AI server backlog and more than 6,500 AI customers. The company expects revenue to grow approximately 70% this fiscal year, according to the report. Part 2 of my Cursor teardown. What I found, and what I’d fix.

The free plan I signed up to on Cursor: Grok 4.6, locked.

When I hit my limit, the chat said “you’re out, Pro $20”. My usage page said “50% used, ₹649”. Same moment, two answers.

Last weekend nearly 9 in 10 upcoming community events were Grok. Today it’s 8 in 10.
Upcoming events in India, Cursor’s 3rd-biggest market: still zero.

Fix 1: make Grok the cheap option, not the locked one. When Microsoft announced the GitHub deal it promised devs “the programming languages, tools and operating systems of their choice.” GitHub kept that, and went from 28M devs to 100M+.

Fix 2: send the volunteers where the sales team is going. Bengaluru, Chennai, Hyderabad, Mumbai. Measure it on free users who move to Start.

If your parent company has a good product, make it the easy pick, not the only pick.

The question I can’t answer: how many Cursor users ever switch away from the default model? If most, the lock is costing sign-ups. If almost none, I’m wrong.

Full teardown in the replies.
